meta.name: Bharti Airtel Ltd
meta.about: Bharti Airtel Ltd is one of the world’s leading providers of telecommunication services with presence in 18 countries representing India, Sri Lanka, 14 countries in Africa. [1]
meta.keyPoints: Segments & Presence[1] Mobile, Broadband, DTH and Bank. The company has operations in India, Africa, Bangladesh and Sri Lanka.
pros: Company has delivered good profit growth of 22.1% CAGR over last 5 years
Company has been maintaining a healthy dividend payout of 48.0%
cons: Stock is trading at 8.32 times its book value
Promoter holding has decreased over last 3 years: -4.68%

growth.text: Revenue compounded at 8.1% a year over 10 years (5y: 16.0%, 3y: 14.9%), from ₹96,532 cr to ₹2,10,973 cr.
Profit grew 17.2% a year over the same decade — faster than revenue, i.e. operating leverage.
Worst profit year: FY20 (-1916.6%); best: FY25 (+338.0%).

margins.text: EBITDA margin has ranged 31.9%–55.2% since FY15 (peak FY26, trough FY19); FY26 was 55.2%.
Q2FY27 operating margin of 57.4% is lower than 1.1% of the 87 quarters on record — near the top of its history.

returns.text: ROE was 25.7% in FY26 (range -41.3–38.3% since FY15).
Stripping out cash and investments, return on operating capital was 21.6% vs headline ROCE of 18.0% — little distortion from the treasury book.
DuPont FY26: net margin 16.0% × asset turnover 0.4x × leverage 4.0x.

cash.text: Over 12 years the business generated ₹6,20,341 cr of operating cash flow (800.6% of reported profit), spent ₹3,56,993 cr on capex and paid ₹44,719 cr in dividends.
FY26 capex was 0.9x depreciation and 22.1% of sales — maintenance-level spending.
Cash conversion cycle of 14 days in FY26.

valuation.text: P/E of 39.1x vs 10-year median 58.7x (range 19.0–321.5x); cheaper than 77.6% of that period.
EV/EBITDA of 11.1x vs 10-year median 9.7x (range 5.8–14.3x); cheaper than 27.4% of that period.
P/B of 8.2x vs 10-year median 5.8x (range 1.6–12.3x); cheaper than 22.2% of that period.
At its 10-year median P/E on current earnings, the stock would be ~₹3,179 vs ₹2,117 today (50.1%).

price.text: Stock up 0.8% over 1 year; 5y CAGR 24.3%, 10y CAGR 22.7%. Currently 2.1% below its all-time high of ₹2,163.
Versus BSE-500: 0.8% vs -10.8% over 1 year; since 2019, 28.8% vs 11.3% a year.

ownership.text: Foreign institutions raised their stake from 22.7% to 25.4% over 12 quarters.
Domestic institutions raised their stake from 19.5% to 21.6% over 12 quarters.
Promoters cut their stake from 54.6% to 50.1% over 12 quarters.
